transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because I keep hearing voices at work. I hear them coming from the call-light speaker and the hallway vents. They keep telling me which patient records have been changed. It sounds as clear as somebody standing right next to me... but it happens even when the unit is completely quiet, and nobody else hears it. So, that's what's going on.
How long have you been hearing these voices—when did they first start?

Well, it's been going on for about two months now. I first started noticing them right around the time I was asked to help lead the new wound-care documentation rollout on the unit. That's when it all began.
Have you been using any alcohol, recreational drugs, or new medications, or do you have any medical conditions like a thyroid problem, seizures, or a head injury around the time these voices started?

No, nothing like that. I don't use drugs or drink, and I haven't started any new medications. As for my health, no, I haven't had any head injuries or seizures... and my thyroid is fine. There's really nothing new physically wrong with me that I know of. It's just these voices.
Since these voices started two months ago, have you noticed any changes in how well you're able to do your job, take care of daily tasks, or interact with coworkers and family?

Yes, it's definitely affected things. I was actually taken off the floor during a shift recently. My supervisor said my handoffs and my charting just weren't safe anymore. And at home, my husband has had to take over a lot of the things I usually handle because I just... I can't. I feel like my reputation at work is completely falling apart, and my plans to go to LPN school are just ruined because of all this.

Besides these voices, have you noticed any other unusual experiences—like strong beliefs others don't share, trouble organizing your thoughts, or a loss of interest and motivation in things you used to enjoy?

Well, there is something else. I don't know if you'd call it a strong belief, but it's the truth. I know the wound-care charts on the unit are showing a pattern that management doesn't want anyone to see. My supervisor keeps telling me it's just late entries or coding mistakes, but... I know better. I can tell they're watching exactly what I write because I'm the one who caught it. I don't have trouble organizing my thoughts or anything, and I still care about things, but I just know they're keeping an eye on me because of those charts.
Since these voices and beliefs started two months ago, have they been present continuously every day, or have there been any breaks where you felt completely back to your normal self?

No, there haven't been any breaks. It's been every day for the last two months. I haven't had a day where I felt like my normal self, or where the voices stopped, or where I didn't feel like I was being watched because of those charts. It's just constant.

Before these voices started two months ago, did you notice any earlier changes—like becoming more withdrawn, having unusual suspicions, or feeling something was 'off'—in the weeks or months leading up to when the voices began?

No, I don't think so. Before two months ago, everything was... well, it was just normal. I was working my regular shifts and doing fine. I wasn't pulling away from people or feeling like anything was off. It really just all started right around that two-month mark. Before that, I was completely myself.

During these past two months, have you also noticed any periods of feeling unusually elated, energetic, or irritable, or on the other end, feeling very depressed or hopeless, that seemed to accompany the voices and beliefs?

Well, I wouldn't say I've felt depressed or hopeless. But... energetic? Yes, definitely. Some days I just feel like I'm finally awake, you know? Like I'm the only one who can see what's going on and I'm meant to fix everything at work. I have all this energy to just get it done. But then, if my husband or one of the nurses tells me to slow down or take a break, I... I get really irritable. I just snap at them. It feels like they're trying to block me from doing something really important, and I just can't stand it when they get in my way.
You mentioned feeling unusually energetic and irritable on some days—can you tell me how many days in a row this elevated, energetic mood has lasted when it occurs?
I'm not really sure about how many days in a row it lasts. I haven't been counting or keeping track like that. It just feels like it's been happening a lot over the last couple of months.

Have there been any days in the past two months when you heard the voices or had the belief about being watched, but did NOT feel that unusually energetic or irritable mood—that is, times the voices/beliefs were present without the mood changes?

No, I don't think so. I mean... I never heard those call-light voices or saw any hidden messages in the patient charts before this whole period started, before I got so driven and wound up about the new rollout at work. 

The voices and the messages really only started happening after I was already sleeping a lot less and working nonstop. That was when I felt so certain that I had to fix everything at the facility. So, no, I haven't had the voices without feeling all that energy and drive. They kind of just go together.
During these energetic periods, have you needed much less sleep than usual but still felt rested and full of energy the next day?

Like I said earlier, I've definitely been sleeping a lot less. But... I'm not really sure if I feel rested, exactly. I haven't really paid attention to that part. 

I just know I wake up after maybe a few hours and my mind is already going over everything I need to fix at the facility. So I just get up and get to it. I don't know if it's because I actually feel rested, I just... I don't seem to need the sleep to keep moving.

Before these past two months, have you ever had another period—at any time in your life—where you felt unusually high-energy, elated, or irritable for several days, or alternatively, a period of deep depression or hopelessness that lasted two weeks or more?

No, I don't think so. I've never had anything like this happen before. I mean, I've had normal ups and downs, like anyone else, but never a time where I was going for days on end like this, or feeling really down and hopeless for weeks. This is all new.

Critically, the psychotic symptoms never occurred independently of the mood disturbance—there were no periods of psychosis without mood symptoms and no prodromal phase of odd behavior preceding the manic symptoms, arguing against a primary psychotic disorder (schizophrenia) or schizoaffective disorder.
